messages:
alex: quick FYI — ran a focused profile on the host ingress path. saw ~12% CPU spent in small write syscalls (writev) during streaming token emit. flame graph attached but TL;DR: hot stack points at ingress_parse -> frame_coalesce -> writev.

ben: ugh, that matches the canary we rolled yesterday. any idea if it's the tokenizer or the streaming layer? :eyes:

alex: initial bisect points to two recent changes: PR #8421 (parser header copy) and a batching tweak in stream-assembler that reduced coalesce window. either could increase syscall churn.

chloe: I pulled a heap profile while reproing with 200 RPS sustained. kvcache eviction spikes line up with write bursts — small fragments cause lots of tiny writes and also blow KV LRU churn.

maria: idea: combine small tokens into a single framed buffer before calling writev. we used a similar micro-optimization in dedicated-runtime and it cut syscall rate by ~60%.

ben: can you paste the perf command you used? I want to run locally.

alex: perf script + FlameGraph (local): 
```
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
perf script > out.perf
stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
open the SVG and search for writev/ingress_parse.

chloe: repro case I used: curl -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" against the local ingress proxy with a streaming prompt load generator (payloads ~300-800 bytes). kvcache key hit-rate dropped ~8% during bursts.

alex: bench numbers: baseline (master before PR #8421) 95 p99 latency 180ms, CPU host-side 22%. after PR + reduced coalesce window: p99 210ms, CPU 28%, syscall rate +2.3x.

maria: rolling back the parser copy seems low-risk. but for a longer-term fix we should: (1) async tokenization thread to batch token writes off the hot path, (2) increase coalesce window adaptively when small-fragment ratio > 30%, (3) add a writev buffer aggregator.

ben: PR #8428 implements an aggregator in stream-assembler — I can wire a flag to enable it on the canary. small patch, no ABI changes.

alex: great — canary that + rollback #8421? would like to isolate. if rollback fixes CPU we still enable aggregator as follow-up.

deploy-bot: deploy requested: eng-runtime/canary -> staging. Triggered by ben. (build: bld-2026-03-19-0912)

chloe: after enabling aggregator on staging i saw write syscall rate drop ~55% and host CPU down ~5%. kvcache hit-rate recovered to within 1% of baseline. p99 improved ~12ms.

ben: nice. open a tracking ticket for adaptive coalesce heuristics and kernel-selection guidance for small-token workloads. also add a microbenchmark to prevent regressions (token small-write workload).

alex: filed RFC and ticket: #RT-1142 (host-side small-write mitigation + tests). linking perf graphs and canary logs in the ticket.

maria: next steps: ship rollback for the copy, enable aggregator by default behind a config, and schedule follow-up for async tokenization design review.

ben: thanks all — nice quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
